beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju bought Kesar Paints at ₹120, and panicked when it stalled at ₹150.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji looked at the chart and smiled.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju sold right when the stock was catching its breath for the next jump.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When price pauses near ₹150 after a sharp rally, it forms a flag or pennant.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy says flags and pennants always fly at half-mast, midway through the move.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Once ₹150 resistance broke on heavy volume, the stock surged to ₹168.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: First, we will master Flags, Pennants, and Rising and Falling Wedges.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Second, we explore Rectangle Trading Ranges and the Measured Move.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Third, we will identify the Continuation Head and Shoulders pattern.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Finally, we test market strength using Confirmation vs. Divergence.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A Flag is a small parallel rectangle that slopes against the prevailing trend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A Pennant uses two converging trendlines, like a tiny symmetrical triangle.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Both share one rule: measure the flagpole and project it from the breakout.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now look at the Wedge: it takes 1 to 3 months with both lines sloping together.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A Rising Wedge narrows upward like this tired climb to ₹148—a bearish sign.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Once ₹140 support broke, price slid to ₹134; conversely, a Falling Wedge is bullish.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A Rectangle is a trading range where buyers and sellers are evenly matched.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Watch volume closely: heavy volume on rallies favors continuation over a reversal.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Once ₹150 breaks, project the ₹10 height of the range upward to ₹160.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The Measured Move says a major advance splits into two equal, parallel legs.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: After the first leg, price retraces a third to half, building a base.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The second leg duplicates the first—add ₹40 from the correction trough.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sometimes a Head and Shoulders pattern continues the trend instead of reversing it.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In an uptrend it is inverted; in a downtrend it stands upright before falling.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Confirmation means price, volume, and indicators all point in the same direction.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When price hits ₹158 but volume or indicators fall, that is Divergence.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Divergence at ₹158 warns us the trend is hollow before price drops to ₹141.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now it is your turn. Read this scenario carefully and identify the pattern.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think: what do two upward-slanting converging lines in a downtrend signal?
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Correct! It is a Bearish Rising Wedge and will break downward to resume the downtrend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In the evening, Raju calculated the exact flag target with Sharma ji.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji advised him to always pair continuation patterns with confirmation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now Raju had the tools both to ride the trend and spot early warnings.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Let us tie together all the key principles of Chapter 6, Part 2.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Flags and pennants are 1-to-3 week pauses that fly at half-mast.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rising wedges are bearish, falling wedges are bullish, and volume decides rectangles.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Measured moves project equal swings, while Continuation H&S extends the trend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Crucial rule: Confirmation vs Divergence: Agreement validates trends; divergence warns of reversals.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Above all, pattern slant and volume confirmation separate true breakouts from traps.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Flags & Pennants: Brief 1-3 week breathers preceded by a sharp flagpole
Half-Mast Rule: Flags and pennants fly midway through the total move
Rising & Falling Wedges: Slant against the trend (Rising = Bearish, Falling = Bullish)
Rectangle Ranges: Horizontal tug-of-war where volume reveals the winner
The Measured Move: Major swings split into two equal legs after a 33%-50% rest
Continuation H&S: Inverted in uptrends, upright in downtrends
Confirmation vs Divergence: Agreement validates trends; divergence warns of reversals
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
